title: Breakfast Stromboli Roll
subtitle: Pizza dough rolled with scrambled eggs, ham, and cheese, baked golden.
description: Pizza dough rolled with scrambled eggs, ham, and cheese, baked golden and sliced into rings. One big roll feeds the hall and reheats clean.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Breakfast Stromboli Roll in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line. Use deli ham as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 425°F. Line a sheet pan with parchment. Stretch each dough ball into a 10x14-inch rectangle on a lightly floured surface, keeping edges slightly thicker.

steps.title: Prep the filling
steps.instruction: Soft-scramble eggs over low heat until just set but still glossy. Spread on a tray to cool 5 minutes—hot eggs will melt cheese prematurely and tear dough.

steps.title: Fill and roll
steps.instruction: Layer ham, scrambled eggs, peppers, and mozzarella on the lower third of each dough rectangle, leaving a 1-inch border. Roll tightly from the bottom, pinch seams closed, and place seam-side down on the pan.

steps.title: Bake until golden
steps.instruction: Brush rolls with olive oil and sprinkle Parmesan. Cut small vents on top. Bake 20–22 minutes until deep golden and internal egg filling reaches 165°F in the center.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Breakfast Stromboli Roll onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.instruction: Rest stromboli 8 minutes before slicing into thick portions with a serrated knife. Serve with warm marinara for dipping at the line.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Breakfast Stromboli Roll — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

stationWorkflow: Cool scrambled eggs slightly before filling—hot filling blows out seams during baking.
Vent the top of each roll so steam escapes and crust stays crisp.
Slice with a serrated knife in one motion to avoid squashing the roll.
cleanupNotes: Use parchment on sheet pans so melted cheese releases without scraping.
Wipe flour from prep surfaces before it mixes with oil and forms paste.
leftovers: Reheat slices on a sheet pan at 375°F for 8 minutes; microwave makes crust rubbery.
Dice leftovers into a breakfast strata with extra eggs and milk for tomorrow's bake.
